collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — ADVICE AND DECISIONS (ADV-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Asking for advice, giving it, ignoring it, following half of it, and deciding alone. Advice can be wrong, even from elders and experts. Following it doesn't guarantee a good outcome and ignoring it doesn't cause a bad one. Feeling heard with no decision is a perfectly good ending, and nobody ever has to admit someone else was right.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

ledger.why: the casting line, carried out as the roles' ages (picks an adult and a healer or elder)

collection.description: On day four of seven days' rest, a villager's knee feels better and the fish are running: go fishing, or stay in.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (friend) told (subject) to rest (subject.his/her) bad knee for seven days. On the fourth day (subject) feels much better. The weather is perfect. The fish are running. (subject.His/her) crew are going out without (subject.him/her). (subject.He/she) stands at the door, looking at (subject.his/her) paddle.

o1__fx.name: Outcome A
o1__fx.text: (subject) goes. The knee is fine all day, mostly. By evening it's a little sore. (subject.He/she) puts it up and says nothing to (friend). Over the next week it heals anyway, maybe slower than it might have, maybe not. There's no way to know. (subject) decides it was worth it for the fish. (friend), finding out, decides not to argue.

o2__fx.name: Outcome B
o2__fx.text: (subject) stays in, grumbling. The crew comes home with a huge catch and tells (subject.him/her) all about it. (subject) is miserable. The knee is completely better by day seven, and (subject.he/she) goes out on day eight. The fish are gone. (subject.He/she) catches nothing. "I followed the advice," (subject.he/she) tells (friend), "and I caught nothing." "The advice was for your knee," says (friend), "not for the fish."
